description:
Per-language MESSAGE TEXT/SHAPE for the shipped 4-class error taxonomy (`AuthenticationError`/`NetworkError`/`MissingKeyError`/`TypeMismatchError`) plus the one Go-only Or-family log line — this is a DIFFERENT concern from `error-mapping.json` (which only proves 'HTTP condition X produces error TYPE Y', not what the message text says). Backfilled per Uma's DX spec flag #6 (`outputs/SPEC-envpit-0t2z-3-1b-ux.md` §2.1: 'Every message below is a vector-suite row... a new error-messages.json family'). Ground truth: sdks/node/src/{errors,client,transport}.ts + sdks/python/src/envpit/{errors,client,transport}.py (both read in full and verified against their real, shipped literal strings — NOT copied from the design doc's proposed copy where the two differ). Go/Java entries are forward-provisioned (design-doc copy, `outputs/SPEC-envpit-0t2z-3-1b-ux.md` §2.2/§1.2/§1.3) — same convention as `hashing.json`: no shipped Go/Java SDK exists yet, so those columns aren't consumed by any test today, reserved so Go/Java prove identical copy from day one once they start.

Per-language copy parity is 'same information, same order, per-language surface convention on top' (ADR-S3-08 lineage) — NOT byte-identical across languages. Node/Python/Java use sentence-case prose; Go uses its own convention (lowercase first word, no trailing period, `envpit:` package prefix). This file's `messages.<language>.message` is each language's own EXACT literal template, not a shared template with substitution.

`{url}` throughout every language's message column below is written literally as the resolved URL a consuming test gets when it explicitly passes `host: "https://example.test"` (`CONFIG_PATH = "/api/v1/config"`) — every language's consuming test for THIS family MUST use that exact host (not its own SDK's default host) so the literal message strings below are directly, byte-for-byte comparable/copy-pasteable into each language's test, matching how sse-frames.json/getters.json embed fully-literal expected values rather than parameterized templates.
notes: Node's `no-api-key-found` case ships a PLAIN `Error` (NOT part of the `EnvpitError` hierarchy) — a known, ALREADY-DOCUMENTED, intentionally-NOT-fixed-here divergence (Uma SPEC-envpit-0t2z-3-1b-ux.md §2.2 flag / §0.1; Sentinel THREATMODEL-envpit-0t2z-3.md). The three new languages use their AuthenticationError-equivalent instead (Uma's recommendation). Node's own alignment is deferred to the coordinated all-4-SDK follow-up tracked at bd:envpit-aw7l — do not 'fix' Node unilaterally from this file or its consuming test.

Exactly ONE documented value-echo carve-out exists in this whole family: `type-mismatch-integer`'s message intentionally includes the raw offending value (`rawValue: "abc"` in the message text) — this is CONFORMANCE.md INV-SDK-11's one documented, accepted exception (shipped-Node parity, ADR-S3-01; Sentinel THREATMODEL-envpit-0t2z-3.md F6). Every OTHER case in this file, INCLUDING the Go-only Or-family log line, is value-free by construction (AC-SEC-SDK3-6) — a consuming language's test SHOULD assert the raw value substring is verifiably ABSENT from every non-carve-out case's message, and present (by design) only in the carve-out case.

`background-refresh-failed-http-500`'s `{msg}` portion is not an independently-authored string — it is composed, end-to-end, from the SAME `NetworkError` produced by the `non-2xx-response` case (case order matters: this is what every real implementation actually emits when a background poll/push refresh's underlying fetch fails with HTTP 500, not a shortcut).

The Go `go-or-family-type-mismatch-value-free` case has no Node/Python equivalent to consume — neither language ships an `Or`-family default-returning getter (Go-only surface, Sara §2.2/R4). Its `languages` field restricts it to `["go"]`; Node/Python consuming tests MUST skip it, not fail it.

Per Uma AC-UX3-03: every produced message must match its language's template verbatim (placeholders substituted) AND contain no config value or API-key substring outside the one documented carve-out above.

cases.name: no-api-key-found
cases.trigger: load() called with no explicit apiKey and no ENVPIT_API_KEY environment variable set

node.message: EnvPit: no API key found. Set the ENVPIT_API_KEY environment variable, or pass { apiKey } to `EnvpitClient.load(...)`.

python.message: EnvPit: no API key found. Set the ENVPIT_API_KEY environment variable, or pass api_key=... to envpit.load().

go.message: envpit: no API key found — set the ENVPIT_API_KEY environment variable, or pass envpit.WithAPIKey(...) to Load

java.message: EnvPit: no API key found. Set the ENVPIT_API_KEY environment variable, or call .apiKey(...) on the builder.

node.message: API key rejected (HTTP 401). It may be revoked, expired, or mistyped. Check Project → API Keys in EnvPit.

python.message: API key rejected (HTTP 401). It may be revoked, expired, or mistyped. Check Project → API Keys in EnvPit.

java.message: API key rejected (HTTP 401). It may be revoked, expired, or mistyped. Check Project → API Keys in EnvPit.

cases.trigger: get(key) called for a key not present in the loaded snapshot and no default supplied

cases.name: background-refresh-failed-http-500
cases.trigger: a background (non-first-load) refresh's underlying fetch fails with the SAME condition as non-2xx-response (HTTP 500) — logged as a warn line, never thrown, per INV-SDK-4

python.message: envpit: background config refresh failed (NetworkError): EnvPit returned HTTP 500 while fetching config from https://example.test/api/v1/config. — serving last known values

cases.name: go-or-family-type-mismatch-value-free
cases.trigger: Go-only: a *Or-family default-returning getter (e.g. GetIntOr) hits a type mismatch — logs a warn line AND surfaces on Errors(ctx), value deliberately OMITTED per AC-SEC-SDK3-6 (unlike type-mismatch-integer's carve-out, this is NEW surface in .3 with no Node-parity excuse to echo the value)
